title: PhotoGuider: Composition-Aware Cropping and 360^{circ} View Framing with Explainable Photographic Assessments

summary: Traditional image cropping assumes the photograph already contains the composition worth keeping, and asks only where to crop. A full 360^{circ} scene offers no such guarantee: the viewing direction in a scene has to be discovered before anything can be framed.
takeaways: On two standard 2D cropping benchmarks, PhotoGuider achieves the highest average mIoU performance against ground-truth crops.
The designed features are extracted using foundation and task-specific vision models and structured into four photographic tokens: Subject, Composition, Aesthetics, and Integrity.
Our MLLM explainer is fine-tuned to generate composition-related explanations conditioned on images and measured token assessments.
